paper.title: Online Two-Sided Markets: Many Buyers Enhance Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated two-sided market (single seller, n buyers), regret w.r.t. optimal SBB mechanism using WBB mechanisms
unmapped: Valuations (b_1..b_n, s) drawn i.i.d. from an arbitrary joint distribution on [0,1]^{n+1}; no independence or density assumption
Mechanism: second-price auction among buyers with reserve price q_t, seller offered price p_t; reward is gain from trade (b_max - s) I(s<=p) I(b_max>=q)
Asymmetric feedback: learner observes all buyer bids >= q_t, and only the one-bit seller acceptance I(s_t<=p_t)
Mechanisms used must be weakly budget balanced each round; comparator is the best fixed strong-budget-balanced reserve price
settings.definition_quote: R_T \coloneq T \cdot \max_{q\in[0,1]}\gft(q)-\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t\in[T]}\gft(q_t)\right], where $q_t$ is the reserve price decided by the learning algorithm at each episode $t$

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated two-sided market, SBB baseline (lower bound)
unmapped: Second-price auction with reserve among n buyers plus fixed seller price; gain-from-trade reward
Asymmetric feedback: buyer bids above reserve observed, one-bit seller feedback
settings.definition_quote: Even if \citet{cesa2024bilateral} provide a the regret lower bound $\Omega(T^{2/3})$ for strong budget balance mechanisms with $1$ buyers, such lower bound can be trivially extended to our setting.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated two-sided market with Global Budget Balance (GBB)
unmapped: Two-dimensional price pair (p,q): seller price p and buyer reserve price q in a second-price auction
Global budget balance constraint: cumulative realized revenue sum_t Rev_t(p_t,q_t) >= 0
Comparator: best fixed price pair maximizing expected gain from trade subject to expected revenue >= 0
Asymmetric feedback: buyer bids above reserve observed, one-bit seller acceptance
Algorithm parameter bar_zeta depends on the distributional assumption (e.g. density bound M)

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained MABs with multi-line feedback graphs and monotone costs
unmapped: Arms a_{i,j}, i in [n] lines, j in [m]; pulling a_{i,j} reveals rewards and costs of all a_{i,k} with k >= j (independence number n)
Monotone costs: c(a_{i,j}) >= c(a_{i,k}) for j<k
Comparator: best arm with expected cost c(a) <= 0; guarantee also on positive cumulative violation sum [c(a_t)]^+
settings.definition_quote: The set of arms $\mathcal{A}$ includes an arm $a_{i,j}$ with $i\in [n]$ and $j\in [m]$ ... When we pull arm $a_{i,j}$, we observe the reward and costs of all arms $a_{i,k}$ for all $k\ge j$. ... c(a_{i,j})\ge c(a_{i,k}) \quad \forall i,j<k.
